description:
Follow-up to the merged canonical-JOB foundation (issue #289 Step 1; PRs #332,
#339, #341, #350, #369). The post-merge code review + blind-spot audit
collected six small, low-risk, independently-revertible cleanups and minor
decisions that don't belong in the bigger follow-up TODOs
(`joinorder-canonical-data-assurance`, `joinorder-redistribution-license-adr`,
`joinorder-accessibility-and-comparability` -- all independent of this one):

  1. `benchbox/core/joinorder/benchmark.py` (~lines 38-47): `JoinOrderBenchmark`
     still carries `csv_delimiter = ","` / `csv_null_marker = ""` class
     attributes and a comment about "data cached before the generator wrote
     manifests" / `resolve_csv_dialect` path (a)/(b). The canonical path
     fetches a pre-built Parquet archive -- there is no generator and no CSV.
     This is dead/misleading code. Remove it (after confirming no loader path
     reads those attrs for the canonical class).

  2. `benchbox/cli/benchmarks.py`: `_estimate_memory_usage["joinorder"] = 0.5`
     (GB) and `_estimate_execution_time["joinorder"] = (10, 30)` predate the
     ~5 GB / 74M-row canonical dataset; there are no `joinorder_synthetic`
     entries (it silently falls back to 1.0 GB / generic). The registry says
     `estimated_time_range: (10, 30)` for joinorder too -- reconcile. Update
     the estimates to reflect the canonical dataset and add `joinorder_synthetic`
     entries.

  3. The `surface: "internal"` contract is only half-enforced. MCP discovery
     (`mcp/tools/discovery.py`), MCP resources, and the explorer honor
     `get_benchmark_surface(...) != "public"` and hide `joinorder_synthetic`.
     The interactive `benchbox` CLI wizard does NOT: `BenchmarkManager._get_available_benchmarks()`
     returns `get_all_benchmarks()` unfiltered and `BENCHMARK_ORDER["Academic"]`
     lists `joinorder_synthetic`, so a user picking "Academic" sees "JoinOrder
     Synthetic" as a selectable option. Decide: either (i) filter the wizard
     by surface so `joinorder_synthetic` is hidden there too, or (ii) define
     "internal" as "hidden from MCP/explorer/programmatic discovery only,
     still interactively runnable" -- and either way document the definition
     next to `get_benchmark_surface` in `benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.py`.

  4. `force_regenerate` on `joinorder` now means "delete and re-download ~1.2 GB
     + re-extract", not "regenerate a 700 KB synthetic dataset". (a) Add a
     size/cost note to the CLI help for the `force_regenerate` option (it's
     registered via `BenchmarkHookRegistry.register_option_specs("joinorder", ...)`
     at the bottom of `benchbox/core/joinorder/benchmark.py`). (b) Verify
     `benchbox/core/data_fetch/` handles concurrent downloads safely -- two
     processes both deciding the archive is absent and both writing the
     `*.part` file -> race / corruption. If `fetch_data` already uses an
     atomic rename + a lockfile, note that; if not, file the race as its own
     finding/TODO (do not fix it here -- out of scope, just surface it).

  5. `_project/joinorder/reference_cardinalities.json` (and the tiny variant)
     use a `first_row_sha256 + row_count + underlying_row_count` format. This
     only works because all 113 JOB queries are single-row `MIN(...)`
     aggregates (so first-row == full result). Add a comment to the generating
     code in `_project/scripts/build_joinorder_data.py` (and a one-line note
     in the JSON-adjacent docs if there's a README) stating this assumption,
     so a future non-aggregate / raw-rows query variant isn't silently
     mis-validated.

  6. `JoinOrder(scale_factor=0.1)` now hard-raises `ValueError`. Saved configs,
     notebooks, `unified_runner` invocations passing a sub-scale break with no
     deprecation window. Decide and RECORD: either (i) "no shim -- a hard
     raise is acceptable for the 0.2.x beta" (likely; just write it in
     `_project/joinorder/migration-plan.md` with the rationale), or (ii)
     implement a one-release warn-and-ignore shim (`scale_factor < 1` -> emit
     a deprecation warning, proceed at 1.0). Default to (i) unless the user
     wants the shim.

Each item is independent; do them as separate work units / commits. Items 1
and 2 are pure code cleanup; 3 has a small decision; 4a is a help-text tweak
and 4b is a read-only audit-or-file; 5 is a comment; 6 is a recorded decision
(or a small shim). Nothing here changes the canonical data or the
scale_factor=1.0-only contract.
